Source availability is a planning expectation, not an entity-by-entity research finding. Families remain indivisible; no periods are researched now.

limitations: All new dossiers are partial: unsupported flags, statistics, currency chronology, exhaustive office lists and succession links are omitted. Researched bounds are editorial coverage, not full state lifetimes.

Company territorial administration, Crown Raj, independent India and Pakistan remain distinct. India before 1947 and Pakistan in 1945 are unresolved raw referents, not independent-state dossiers. Existing enriched Raj facts are untouched.

Ceylon’s coastal and post-convention administrations are separate. Legislative/State Council and independent Ceylon have their own intervals. Dutch Ceylon in 1800 is anachronistic after the documented 1796 acquisition; no guessed alternative mapping. Sri Lanka-labelled 1945 maps to dated colonial Ceylon, and 1960 to independent Ceylon, not the post-1972 republic.

Sikkim’s 1815 wartime raw identity remains review; a useful 1818–1827 treaty-era dossier is available between snapshots but is not counted as 1815 availability. Bahawalpur’s 1800 political framework remains unresolved despite evidence of an earlier Nawabi city; 1802/1833 institutions are not projected back.

Maratha Confederacy cannot be flattened into a Peshwa sovereign template from a 1817 museum reference. Full state gazetteer bodies failed repeatedly, and search snippets were not used as factual evidence. The 1800/1815 composite referents remain review.

Sindh’s multiple Talpur branches and Hyderabad’s capital are documented; which branch or composite the 1800 raw identity denotes remains review. No geometry-derived assignment to Hyderabad, Khairpur or Mirpur.

Qajar royal and constitutional frameworks and Pahlavi practical frameworks are separately dated. No new state is manufactured from Persia/Iran naming. 1906–1918, the 1921 coup aftermath, 1925 transition gap, 1941 wartime changes and 1949–1957 institutions remain uncurated.

Afghan 1922/1923 first-constitution precision conflicts are not guessed. Accepted 1920 curation precedes them. Earlier 1800/1815/1878, 1880 accession and 1930 transition remain gaps; formal 1931 bicameralism is distinguished from royal predominance.

Bhutan’s treaty advice clauses are not treated as annexation or an unrestricted-sovereignty claim. Named later rulers and legislature remain uncurated. Nepal’s 1948 draft is not treated as operative then, nor the later 1962 Panchayat constitution projected into 1960.

Goa’s British garrison is described under Portuguese administration; no exact 1815 withdrawal date or sovereign transfer is invented. Awadh and Hyderabad have narrow royal-government profiles; treaty and external-status research remains incomplete.

Travancore treaty clauses describe distinct 1795/1805 arrangements, not continuous effective internal government across conflicts. Cochin’s 1791 clauses apply to stated possessions, not automatic proof of whole-territory sovereignty. Madras civil-judicial proposals are not recorded as accomplished reforms.

Excluded Bangladesh, Central Asian Khanates and Turan remain unresolved/excluded. Chronology, multiple distinct khanates and a geographic label do not independently resolve the exact upstream referents. No denominator or membership changes.
